chunks: And this hadith was narrated to me by Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Isam al-Kulayni, Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Imran al-Daqqaq, Ali ibn Abdullah al-Warraq, Al-Hasan ibn Ahmad al-Mu'addib, and Al-Husayn ibn Ibrahim ibn Hisham al-Mu'addib - may God be pleased with them - who said: He narrated to us Muhammad ibn Yaqub al-Kulayni, who said: He narrated to us Muhammad al-Qasim ibn al-Ala, who said: He narrated to us Al-Qasim ibn Muslim, from his brother Abd al-Aziz ibn Muslim, from Al-Rida (peace be upon him).

key_terms.الدَّقَّاقُ: Al-Daqqaq (a scholar known for his expertise)
key_terms.الْوَرَّاقُ: Al-Warraq (a scholar known for his work with manuscripts)
key_terms.رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمْ: May God be pleased with them (a phrase of approval for narrators)

ai.seo_question: Who are the narrators in the chain for this hadith from Al-Rida?
ai.summary: This isnad traces the transmission of a key hadith on Imamate through the scholarly network of Shaykh al-Saduq, linking the teachings of Imam al-Rida (AS) to the broader corpus of Shia hadith literature via figures like al-Kulayni. It highlights the interconnectivity between major hadith compilers, emphasizing the reliability and scholarly consensus surrounding the divine leadership (Imamah) and its nobilities.
